subject: ich
title: Model Question Paper 1
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–20 are MCQs (1 mark each). Section B: questions 21–35 are objective questions of 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each).
Section C: questions 36–40 carry 2 marks (about 25 words); Section D: questions 41–45 carry 3 marks (40–50 words); Section E: questions 46–50 carry 5 marks (150–200 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, one word or phrase, match).

questions.q: Mark true or false: (a) Culture is not the way of life. (b) Culture is the embodiment of the way in which we think and do things.
Fill in the blanks: The Bhakti and ______ movements emerged in medieval India. Both held that ______ is supreme and all men are equal to him.
Answer in a phrase: (a) Why did reformers use novels, dramas and poetry? (b) Why did reformers use Indian languages?
questions.answer: (a) To reach and awaken the common people. (b) To make their message understood by the masses.

questions.q: Give reasons in short phrases: Why do the scripts of Hindi, Gujarati and Punjabi bear similarities? Give two reasons.
questions.answer: All three originated from the old Brahmi script; they changed slowly over a long period from the same source.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) ______ Despatch of 1854 led to universities. (b) The three universities of Calcutta, Madras and Bombay were established in ______.
Fill in the blanks: In the ______ century and especially after 1919 the ______ national movement became the main propagator of social reforms.
Mark true or false: (a) Religious reforms among Sikhs were started in the twentieth century. (b) The Khalsa College of Amritsar was founded in 1892.
questions.answer: (a) False – they began at the end of the 19th century. (b) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Mithila paintings are made on ______ treated paper with vegetable colours and finished in ______ lines.
Mark true or false: (a) Warli painting uses religious iconography. (b) Phad is a scroll painting.
questions.answer: (a) False – it is a secular art form. (b) True.

questions.q: Mark true or false: (a) Kathak was promoted by Muslim rulers in the medieval period. (b) Aurangzeb was a great patron of Kathak.
Answer in a phrase: (a) What were the two functions of karkhanas? (b) Name two subjects in the primary curriculum.
questions.answer: (a) Manufacturing and technical–vocational training. (b) Arithmetic and mensuration (also geometry, agriculture).

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) How did Vikram Sarabhai save crores of rupees? (b) Name two institutions he founded.
questions.answer: (a) By manufacturing military hardware and antibiotics and penicillin in India. (b) Indian Institutes of Management; the Ahmedabad Textile Industry research association (TERLS also).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Learning in the Gurukul began with the ______ ceremony. The relationship was called the ______ parampara.
Mark true or false: (a) Joint families may be matrilineal in Kerala. (b) Hindu Acts of 1955–56 govern Muslims.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – they govern Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs and Jains.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in about 25 words.

questions.q: Write any two brief characteristic features of Patachitras.
questions.answer: They are mostly painted on cloth and are highly detailed, similar to the Kalighat pats; they depict religious and mythological themes.

questions.q: What was the contribution of Baz Bahadur and Rupmati to music?
questions.answer: The legendary ruler of Malwa and his wife introduced new ragas.

questions.q: Name any two Persian medical works of the medieval period.
questions.answer: Tibb-i-Firozshahi, Tibbi Aurangzebi, Majiny-e-Diyae and Mualajat-i-Dara Shikohi.

questions.q: How did Kalam's research help the polio-affected?
questions.answer: Light carbon material designed for Agni reduced the weight of calipers from 4 kg to 400 g.

questions.q: How does the Right to Education Act help in the spread of education in India?
questions.answer: It makes elementary education free and compulsory for children aged 6–14 in a neighbourhood school; local authorities identify drop-outs and admit them in age-appropriate classes with special training.

or.q: Explain how school management or local authorities can help in implementing the RTE Act.
or.answer: They identify drop-outs and out-of-school children above six years and admit them to classes appropriate to their age after special training.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 40–50 words.

questions.q: Explain the link between culture and heritage.
questions.answer: Culture develops through history as ancestors add and drop traits; what we inherit from them is our cultural heritage, which includes monuments, artefacts, knowledge, philosophy and scriptures; culture may change but the heritage remains.

questions.q: Explain the main features of the Bhakti movement.
questions.answer: Oneness of God and brotherhood of all human beings without discrimination of caste or gender; surrender to God, who is all-pervasive; intense personal devotion with a good moral life; the guru as spiritual guide with the pahul system; condemned rituals and sacrifices and used local languages.
questions.note: April 2022 (8 marks) asked for the development of the Bhakti movement. Lesson 4.

questions.q: Mention any three features of the education system under the Mughals.
questions.answer: Education through pathshalas, vidyapeeths, makhtabs and madrasas; temples and mosques as centres of elementary education teaching Sanskrit and Persian, supported by donations; Akbar added accountancy, public administration and geometry, gave grants and built a workshop; no formal women's education.

questions.q: Explain the four purusharthas and ashramas.
questions.answer: The aims of life are dharma, artha, kama and moksha. For these a life is divided into brahmacharya (education), grihastha (family life and livelihood), vanaprastha (retirement and detachment) and sanyasa (renunciation).

questions.q: Describe India's contacts with the Roman Empire.
questions.answer: In the first three centuries AD, South India had profitable sea trade with Rome, exporting pepper, spices, gems, pearls, ivory, silk and muslin; Roman coins were found at Coimbatore and Madurai; trade brought gold and gave the Kushanas a stable gold currency; yavanas guarded Tamil kings and ports at Sopara, Broach and Kaveripattinam handled the trade.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 150–200 words.

questions.q: Explain the development of the Bhakti movement and its role in enriching Indian culture.
questions.answer: Islam's message of equality challenged the rigid caste society and gave rise to the Bhakti movement (14th–16th centuries). Saints from Alvars and Nayanars in the south, Ramanuja, Ramananda, Kabir, Nanak, Chaitanya, Mirabai, Namdev, Tulsidas and Surdas taught the oneness of God, devotion over ritual, equality and brotherhood. It split into nirguna and saguna streams. Their poetry in local languages (geet, qawali) united people and stimulated regional languages; Sikhism grew out of its nirguna branch.

questions.q: Describe the impact of the British on the Indian economy.
questions.answer: The British first took hold of trade, buying cheap from peasants through Seths and gomastas; then controlled production to suit exports and destroyed Indian industries; after Plassey they monopolised cotton and imposed heavy duties on Indian goods in Britain. By 1813 India was a consumer of British goods and supplier of raw materials; railways, steamships and telegraph served British trade. Indian handicrafts faced extinction.

questions.q: Explain the contribution of Christian missionaries and the press to Indian languages and literature.
questions.answer: Missionaries produced dictionaries and grammars (e.g. William Carey's Bengali grammar and dictionary), introduced lithographic presses that published local-language books and journals, and opened schools and colleges teaching local languages. This created an educated class that wanted to read, enriched vocabulary with new words and helped literature, newspapers and nationalism to grow.

questions.q: Write about the impact of the reform movements on Indian society.
questions.answer: Laws were passed against sati (1829), infanticide, for widow remarriage (1856), inter-caste marriage (1872) and the Sharda Act (1929). After 1919 the national movement propagated reform using Indian languages, novels, drama, the press and the cinema; women's education grew and purdah and child marriage declined, women joined the freedom struggle and many superstitions disappeared.

questions.q: Explain the contribution of the Mughals to painting.
questions.answer: The Mughals began a new era by synthesising Indian painting with the Persian tradition. Humayun brought Persian painters; Akbar patronised Hindu and Persian artists, recorded their names and produced illustrated manuscripts and portraits; Jahangir, himself a connoisseur, took the art to its zenith with vibrant colours and a three-dimensional effect, while Mansur painted birds and animals; Dara Shikoh patronised painting; Mughal court painters introduced landscapes with human figures and signed miniatures.
